page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the n2 server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks place the n2-highmem-8 in the average tier for most memory and general compute operations. The passmark memory score and memory bandwidth tests, including read-only small block cached at 413.33 GB/sec and large block uncached write at 40.05 GB/sec, rank in the middle 50%. However, multi-core processing efficiency shows limitations, with geekbench multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scores falling into the bottom 25%. Large-model LLM inference is a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a medium 7B model registering in the bottom 10% at 10.36 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-8 offers a high resource density of memory relative to compute cores, making it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The hardware is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and static web serving, where its average database operations and static web serving throughput of 7.05 GB/sec can be fully utilized. It is less optimal for compute-heavy tasks like ray tracing, image processing, or large language model inference.
